chunks: On the first day of Dhu al-Hijjah, Ibrahim, the Friend of the Most Merciful, peace be upon him, was born. Whoever fasts on that day, it will be an expiation for sixty years. And on the ninth of Dhu al-Hijjah, the repentance of Dawud, peace be upon him, was sent down. Whoever fasts on that day, it will be an expiation for ninety years.

key_terms.إِبْرَاهِيمُ: Ibrahim عليه السلام, the Prophet described here as born on the first of Dhu al-Hijjah
key_terms.تَوْبَةُ دَاوُدَ: the repentance of Dawud عليه السلام, described as accepted on the ninth of Dhu al-Hijjah
key_terms.تِسْعِينَ سَنَةً: ninety years, indicating the magnitude of the expiatory reward
key_terms.خَلِيلُ الرَّحْمَنِ: the intimate friend of the Most Merciful, a title for Ibrahim عليه السلام
key_terms.ذِي الْحِجَّةِ: Dhu al-Hijjah, the sacred month in which these virtuous days occur
key_terms.صَامَ: fasted; observed sawm on the specified day
key_terms.كَفَّارَةَ: expiation; a means of atonement for sins

ai.seo_question: What is the reward for fasting on the first and ninth days of Dhu al-Hijjah?
ai.summary: This hadith describes the merit of fasting on specific days in Dhu al-Hijjah. It links the first day to the birth of Ibrahim عليه السلام and the ninth day to the acceptance of the repentance of Dawud عليه السلام, emphasizing the immense expiatory reward attached to fasting on those days.

en.bab-ul-qaim-publications: "On the first day of Dhu al-Hijjah, Ibrahim, the Friend of the Most Merciful (as), was born. Whoever fasts on that day, it will be an expiation for sixty years. On the ninth of Dhu al-Hijjah, the repentance of Dawud (as) was accepted. Whoever fasts on that day, it will be an expiation for ninety years."
